messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — I ran an nsys timeline on the small-batch workload and saw a big spike whenever batch_size == 1. The timeline is full of extremely short CUDA kernels interleaved with NVTX ranges per token. Looks like we’re paying for instrumentation and kernel-selection churn. Anyone else hit this?

maya: Yep saw that in a reproduce run yesterday. I suspect two things: (1) we emit NVTX ranges inside the inner token loop (one per token op), and (2) kernel selector logic runs per token because sequence-length heuristics keep flipping. Both add overhead.

cheng: Can you paste the nsys command you used? I want the trace to grep the kernel names.

alex:
```
nsys profile -o smallbatch.nsys --trace=nvtx,cuda,cudnn --sample=none ./bench_small_batch
nsys stats smallbatch.nsys
```
The timeline clearly shows repeated tiny kernels like matmul_fwd_1, softmax_kernel_2, then an NVTX range named "token-op:kv_prefetch:req=..." for each token.

sam: For context: why are we putting NVTX in the inner loop? We wanted per-token visibility for debugging KV prefetch ordering. But at scale that creates hundreds of ranges per request. NVTX itself is cheap but the timeline/event overhead and serialization to the tracer is costly.

olga: Agreed. Two tradeoffs: observability vs tracer noise. We should keep request-level spans and coarse-grain some inner spans. E.g., one NVTX span for the whole token loop with attributes summarizing counts, and only sample detailed token spans for 1% of requests.

maya: Proposal for naming lexicon (kinda draft):
- request-level: r:request/<req_id> (push at request start, pop at end)
- batch-level: r:batch/<model>-bs<bs>
- kernel-level: k:<kernel_name> (only for heavyweight kernels > X ms)
- kv ops: kv:prefetch / kv:insert (token idx as attr, but not separate range per token by default)
Keep names short to avoid long labels on timeline.

cheng: I like short names. Also add structured tags into the NVTX message so we can grep them from traces: e.g. "r:req=abcd model=gpt-4x bs=1 seq=32". Key names: req, model, bs, seq, tok, kernel_hint.

alex: Example NVTX macros we used:
```c
#define PUSH_REQ(rid, model, bs) nvtxRangePushExA( /* name */ namebuf)
// namebuf = fmt("r:req=%s model=%s bs=%d", rid, model, bs)
```
We were doing PUSH_TOKEN(...) inside token loop. Plan: move PUSH_TOKEN to be conditional on sampling.

sam: Another regression cause: kernel selector code calls a small heuristic function that grabs a global config lock when it runs. If that fires per token for bs=1 that serializes CPU threads and delays enqueuing kernels. Might explain extra kernel splits. We should memoize selector output for the current request/sequence length/model combination.

olga: +1 for memoization and lock-free reads. Also we should add an attribute on request-span to record which kernel variant was chosen (kernel_variant=matmul_f32_q2 etc.) so post-mortems can correlate variant -> latency.

maya: Perfetto: for longer term analysis we should export nsys -> perfetto so we can do aggregated views. But immediate mitigations: (1) stop per-token NVTX by default, (2) sample detailed per-token traces 1/100 or 1/1000, (3) memoize kernel selection per request, (4) coalesce KV operations in NVTX when contiguous.

cheng: One more nuance: KV cache behavior. If we prefetch per token we sometimes trigger a writeback path that invalidates small portions of the cache, causing eviction churn. On timeline it looks like tiny memcpy kernels scattered across. We should instrument KV operations but as a batched label: e.g., "kv:prefetch count=8 bytes=64k" instead of 8 separate ranges.

alex: CI bot actually alerted a perf regression earlier this week: ci-bot: "perf-regression: latency +11% on small-batch benchmark (job 1022)" (link: https://ci.example/reports/1022). The change that introduced per-token NVTX is in runtime commit abc123.

ci-bot: reg-alert: job=1022 baseline=20.1ms new=22.3ms delta=+11% suspect=runtime/trace(abc123)

sam: Actionable items:
- alex: create a minimal PR that moves NVTX request->outer loop and converts per-token ranges to sampled detailed spans.
- cheng: add memoization for kernel selector (thread-local cache keyed by (model, seq_len, bs) with TTL per request).
- maya: update naming doc in repo (short lexicon + attributes). I'll stub a README under /docs/instrumentation.
- olga: add study job to run nsys profiles with and without changes and attach perf counters (SM occupancy, memcpy overhead).

olga: Quick instrumentation example we agreed on: one request span, an inner synthesized counter and sampled token spans. Pseudocode: 
```c
PUSH_REQ(rid, model, bs, seq);
for (tok=0; tok<seq; tok++) {
  if (sampled) PUSH_TOKEN(tok);
  kv_prefetch_batch_if_needed(tok);
}
POP_REQ();
```
And NVTX labels short: "r:req=abcd m=gpt4x bs=1 s=32" and "k:matmul v=2"

alex: Who wants to own the PR for the selector memoization?

cheng: I'll pick it up. Will add a small benchmark to ensure lock-free reads do not regress.

sam: OK. Once we have memoization + NVTX relocation, run a 1000-run small-batch job and compare percentiles. If regression goes away we should roll back token-level NVTX permanently.

maya: Also add a doc note: NVTX is for human debugging; don’t rely on it for production metrics. Use structured logs/metrics for long-term dashboards.

alex: Thanks everyone — leaving checklist in the PR. I’ll attach the nsys capture to the ticket. :thumbsup:

cheng: :eyes: will follow up with selector patch review later today.
